learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of reporting what someone else said without using their exact words, just like a news reporter!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Direct speech gives the exact, word-for-word quote of what someone said. We always trap their words inside quotation marks. Example: Rohan said, 'I am hungry.' You are repeating his exact voice!

Indirect speech (or Reported Speech) is when you tell someone else what was said, but without using the exact quotes. Example: Rohan said THAT he was hungry. You removed the quotes and explained his idea.
To change Direct to Indirect, first remove the commas and quotation marks. Then, use the magic glue word 'THAT' to connect the sentences. 'She said, I am happy' becomes 'She said THAT...'
You have to change pronouns so the story makes sense. If Priya says, 'I like my dress', you report it by saying: Priya said that SHE liked HER dress. 'I' becomes 'She', and 'My' becomes 'Her'.

main_concepts.concept_title: ⏳ Rule 3: The Time Travel Rule (Tense Shift)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Because you are reporting something that was said in the past, the tense usually takes one step back into the past! Simple Present becomes Simple Past ('I play' -> 'He played'). 'Is/Am/Are' become 'Was/Were'. Can becomes Could, and Will becomes Would.

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Gossip Reporter
fun_activity.instructions: Pretend you are a news reporter. Your friend says: 'I will buy a new bicycle tomorrow.' Turn this Direct quote into an Indirect report using 'He/She said that...'

quick_recap: ⭐ Direct speech uses exact words inside quotation marks.
⭐ Indirect speech reports the meaning without quotes, often using the word 'that'.
⭐ When changing to indirect speech, pronouns change to match the speaker.
⭐ Tenses take a step back into the past (Present becomes Past).
⭐ Time words change too! 'Today' becomes 'that day', and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.
